image.alt: A black rubber plant with glossy deep burgundy leaves and red midribs, in a white pot

light.label: Bright indirect light
light.note: Tolerates gentle morning sun and medium light

landscape_use.note: Frost-free zones only; keep it in a pot, as in the ground it becomes a very large tree

home_use.note: Choose a bright spot and keep it there; it dislikes sudden changes

snap: An upright rubber plant with large, glossy, deep burgundy-black leaves and red midribs. New leaves unfurl from a bright red bud. It is sturdy, slow-growing and easy to keep. Toxic to cats and dogs if chewed, and the milky sap irritates skin.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: The rubber plant is native to the forests of South and Southeast Asia, where it grows into a huge tree with aerial roots. The Burgundy is a cultivated form with very dark leaves. Indoors it grows slowly to 1–2 m, with a single upright stem and big, leathery leaves.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Give it bright indirect light, and a little gentle morning sun is fine. In dim light the dark colour fades and the plant stretches. Water when the top 3–5 cm of soil is dry, and never leave the pot standing in water. Too much water makes the leaves yellow and drop. Keep it above 12°C and away from cold drafts.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: The leaves are almost black, with a glossy shine and a red midrib that catches the light. Each new leaf opens from a bright red bud sheath that later drops off. Wipe the leaves with a damp cloth to keep them shiny. It can be pruned to control its height, and pruning makes it branch.
